What is the correct modern way to load a Google Font in HTML? Show the full pattern.

```html
<head>
  <!-- Warm up the connection to the font CDN -->
  <link rel='preconnect' href='https://fonts.googleapis.com'>
  <link rel='preconnect' href='https://fonts.gstatic.com' crossorigin>
  <!-- Load the CSS, then the fonts -->
  <link href='https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@400;700&display=swap' rel='stylesheet'>
</head>
```

```css
body {
  font-family: 'Inter', system-ui, sans-serif;
}
```

Why it works: fonts.googleapis.com serves the CSS and fonts.gstatic.com serves the actual .woff2 files — preconnect opens DNS + TCP + TLS to both hosts in parallel with HTML parsing, saving several round trips. The crossorigin attribute is required on the gstatic preconnect because font requests are CORS requests. display=swap tells the browser to show fallback text immediately and swap in the webfont when ready.

How do variable fonts work with Google Fonts and the weight range syntax? Show an example with Inter.

```html
<link rel='preconnect' href='https://fonts.googleapis.com'>
<link rel='preconnect' href='https://fonts.gstatic.com' crossorigin>
<link href='https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@100..900&display=swap' rel='stylesheet'>
```

```css
body { font-family: 'Inter', system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 400; }
h1   { font-weight: 800; }
.legal { font-weight: 300; } /* any value 100-900 is valid */
```

Why it works: the wght@100..900 syntax requests the variable font file, which contains the entire weight axis in a single .woff2 instead of one file per weight. The browser can then render any weight in that range continuously — including values like 550 that do not exist as static fonts. One request, one file, unlimited weights; that is usually smaller overall than downloading 3-4 separate static weights.

I need two font families on one page. What is the most efficient way to request them from Google Fonts?

```html
<!-- One CSS request carries both families and all weights -->
<link rel='preconnect' href='https://fonts.googleapis.com'>
<link rel='preconnect' href='https://fonts.gstatic.com' crossorigin>
<link href='https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@400;700&family=JetBrains+Mono:wght@400;600&display=swap' rel='stylesheet'>
```

```css
body { font-family: 'Inter', system-ui, sans-serif; }
pre, code { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; }
```

Why it works: multiple family parameters in a single css2 URL produce one CSS response that declares both families, so the browser makes one request for the stylesheet instead of two. The .woff2 files themselves are still fetched individually per family/weight, but only when a weight is actually used on the page. Efficiency checklist: combine families in one URL, list only weights you use, add display=swap, preconnect to both hosts, and give every family a matching fallback keyword (sans-serif, monospace) so text renders even if the network fails.
